threads.body: `resp.flushBuffer()` can throw `IOException`, and calling it after `writer.close()` may be less reliable on some servlet containers (the response/writer may be considered closed, causing the flush to fail and potentially mask the intended `IllegalStateException`). Consider flushing before closing (e.g., `writer.flush(); resp.flushBuffer();`) and then closing if needed, or handle any `IOException` from `flushBuffer()` so this branch still deterministically throws the intended exception.
